newsitem.title: GERMANY: German Ifo institute plans confidence index revamp.
newsitem.headline: German Ifo institute plans confidence index revamp.

text.p: Germany's Ifo research institute said it planned to revamp its highly respected consumer climate index to better reflect the state of business confidence after German unification.

From March, the Munich-based institute plans to release its monthly business confidence numbers for east and west Germany to show a change from month-ago numbers rather than giving an index number which is compared with the base year, 1991.

Ifo officials said the change was necessary after east and west German data had become wildly skewed, following the east German states' post-unification upswing and the western states' deep recession.

Consequently the east German figures had been much higher in absolute terms than the west German figures, indicating the struggling eastern states were actually faring better than businesses in the western part of the nation.
For example the January index showed west German confidence at 93.3 points while the east German index was at 106.6 points.

Economists said these numbers, hotly anticipated by financial markets every month, could lead to great confusion as they no long reflected conditions. But economists also reserved judgement on the new system, predicting the switchover could create chaos and similarly confusing statistics at the outset.

Every month the Ifo institute polls 7,000 companies on their outlook for business dividing responses into "good", "satisfactory" or "poor". Sorted by industry, the answers were then weighted and reported separately as west and east German business condidence indeces.

Now the survey will be based on the addition of balances. For example, if out of 100 surveyed companies 50 said the outlook would be unchanged, 30 said it would be better and 20 said it would be worse, the balance would then be that 10 companies were more optimistic.

From now on the higher the actual number, the more companies were tipping for improved conditions. If however all 100 companies were to expect poor conditions, the balances could slump to minus 100, indicating gloomy conditions.
Ifo will then tabulate balances for east and west Germany, coming up with "Business climate balances for West and East Germany."
To smooth the switchover, Ifo said it planned to release the February data, expected around March 20, under both the old index and the new balances systems.
